title: Esra and the Cosmic Shield
markdown:
Sunlight hit Esra’s window. The water was too close. The flood had changed Tidehaven. Damp, chilly air. Esra blinked awake. The water was right there. Her black cat, Mica, was a bundle of jitters. Tail twitching. Golden eyes wide.

Thump-thump-thump. Boots on the porch. Captain Noor, the town engineer, burst in. “Esra! Move. The tide’s fast. Our old seawall is failing.” Her voice was tight. The town’s blunt defences were crumbling.

Esra’s mind raced. Astronomy. How worlds handle what hits them. Earth’s magnetic field does not punch the solar wind. It curves, spreads, peels the blow aside. The atmosphere does not stand like a brick. It thickens, slows, spends the energy of small falling stones. A shield that works with the hit, not against it as a flat slap.

The old seawall was a slap. Vertical. Water crashed, climbed, tore.

“Captain.” An idea, hot and fast. “The wall is straight. The water has nowhere to go but through it. We need a slope. A curve the wave can run up, so it spends itself instead of punching. Not a dish that focuses — that would gather the force to a point. A face that spreads it. And the roads — not solid slabs. Permeable paving. Let the water sink, not pond.”

Captain Noor squinted at the napkin sketch, then at the churning sea. Doubt flickered. Esra’s conviction did not. “You think this cosmic geometry can save Tidehaven?”

“It’s physics. The same idea as a planetary shield. Deflect. Spread. Drain. Don’t meet a surge with a cliff.” Mica let out a soft mrrrow, as if he understood.

“All right, Esra. Less than two hours. You’re in charge. My team is ready. Let’s build this cosmic shield.”

Action exploded. Cranes groaned. Diggers roared. Esra, clipboard tight, darted among workers. They set curved, sloped modules to let the water climb and turn. Permeable stones went down with care. Mica watched from a dry crate. The air thrummed.

Then it hit. The surge. A wall of water smashed the new face. Instead of a boom, a deep rumbling hum. The water ran up the curve, lost its punch, spilled aside. On the porous roads it trickled through and vanished harmlessly instead of sheet-flooding the street.

Captain Noor stood silent, watching the receding roar. A long breath. A grin. “It worked. Esra — you’ve built resilience. You’ve shown us how to work with the water.”

Esra beamed. Warmth brighter than sunrise. Mica stretched, grooming, calm restored. “The universe has better blueprints than a brick wall,” she whispered. “We just have to look up. And around.”

She did not declare the day amazing. She watched the quieted harbour, and wondered what else a shield might be, if it learned to bend.
characters: Esra (an astronomy intern), Mica (a cat), Noor (a captain)
